_note: MOCK baselines for testing the scoring logic only. Illustrative early-career profiles drafted from common job-posting patterns; not validated against market data. Edit freely in the Baselines page.

baselines.title: AI Engineer
baselines.scope_expectation: Owns well-defined features or components end to end (e.g. a retrieval pipeline, an evaluation harness, a model-serving endpoint) within a team; works with a senior engineer on design; ships to staging or production.
baselines.complexity_criteria: Built or integrated an ML/LLM system beyond a tutorial: e.g. combined retrieval with a model, handled evaluation or failure cases, dealt with latency/cost limits, data quality issues, or deployment constraints.
baselines.description: Early-career AI Engineer who builds and ships applications on top of machine learning and large language models: prompt and retrieval pipelines, evaluation, APIs and basic deployment. Works in Python with modern ML tooling and collaborates with product and data teams.

criteria.name: Machine learning fundamentals
criteria.description: Training, validating and evaluating models; understanding overfitting, metrics and data splits.

criteria.name: LLM application development
criteria.description: Building applications that call large language models: prompting, structured output, tool use, chaining.

criteria.name: Retrieval-augmented generation
criteria.description: Embedding documents, vector search and feeding retrieved context to a model.

criteria.name: Model evaluation
criteria.description: Designing test sets and metrics to measure model or LLM output quality.

criteria.name: API development
criteria.description: Building and consuming REST APIs to serve or integrate models.

criteria.name: Data preprocessing
criteria.description: Cleaning, transforming and preparing data for models.

criteria.name: Fine-tuning
criteria.description: Adapting pretrained models to a task with additional training.

criteria.name: Cloud ML certification
criteria.description: E.g. AWS Machine Learning or Google Cloud ML Engineer certification.

baselines.title: Data Scientist
baselines.scope_expectation: Owns an analysis or model for a defined business question within a team: frames the question, prepares data, builds and evaluates the model, and presents findings to stakeholders.
baselines.complexity_criteria: Worked with messy or multi-source data, chose and justified a method (e.g. experiment design, forecasting, classification), handled evaluation and trade-offs, and connected results to a business decision.
baselines.description: Early-career Data Scientist who turns data into decisions: exploratory analysis, statistical modeling, experimentation and machine learning, communicated clearly to non-technical stakeholders.

criteria.name: Statistical analysis
criteria.description: Hypothesis testing, regression, confidence intervals, distributions.

criteria.name: Machine learning
criteria.description: Building supervised/unsupervised models and evaluating them.

criteria.name: Exploratory data analysis
criteria.description: Profiling data and finding patterns before modeling.

criteria.name: Data visualization and communication
criteria.description: Presenting findings with charts and clear narratives for stakeholders.

criteria.name: Data science or analytics certification
criteria.description: E.g. a cloud data/ML certification or a recognized analytics certificate.

baselines.title: Product Manager
baselines.scope_expectation: Owns a feature or small product area: defines the problem, writes requirements, prioritizes with engineering and design, ships, and measures the result.
baselines.complexity_criteria: Handled ambiguity and trade-offs across stakeholders: e.g. prioritized competing requests, used user research or data to choose a direction, managed scope against constraints, and measured outcome after launch.
baselines.description: Early-career Product Manager (APM/PM) who discovers user problems, defines requirements, works with engineering and design to ship, and measures impact with data.

criteria.name: Product discovery and user research
criteria.description: Interviews, surveys and usability tests to understand user problems.

criteria.name: Requirements writing
criteria.description: PRDs, user stories and acceptance criteria.

criteria.name: Prioritization
criteria.description: Using frameworks or data to decide what to build next.

criteria.name: Product analytics
criteria.description: Defining metrics and analyzing usage to make decisions.

criteria.name: Cross-functional collaboration
criteria.description: Working with engineering, design and business stakeholders to ship.

criteria.name: Technical fluency
criteria.description: Understanding APIs, data and system trade-offs well enough to work with engineers.

criteria.name: Product management certification
criteria.description: E.g. a recognized product management or agile certificate.
